title: Chicken Chettinad
subtitle: South Indian chicken curry with bold spicing
excerpt: Chettinad cooking comes from the Chettinad region of Tamil Nadu and is known for its fiery, aromatic spicing. Fennel seeds, coriander seeds, and whole spices are ground fresh for each cook. This is a deeply flavoured, dry-style curry -- more spice paste than sauce.
sourceNotes: The Chettiar merchant community of Tamil Nadu developed one of the most complex spice cuisines in India over centuries of trade. Chettinad dishes are characterised by freshly ground spice pastes, kalpasi (stone flower), and marathi mokku (dried flower pods), though this version uses more accessible substitutes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The spice paste can be made 1 day ahead and kept refrigerated.

content.text: Dry-roasting the whole spices before grinding makes a real difference. Do it in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant. Let them cool before grinding, or the steam will make the paste clump.

items.prepNote: use 4 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed

content.text: Dry-roast the fennel seeds, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, cardamom pods, and cloves in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant. Cool, then grind to a powder.
Blend the garlic, ginger, and ground spices with 3 tablespoons of water to make a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pan. Fry the shallots over medium heat for 12 minutes until deep golden. Do not rush this step.
Add the spice paste and chilli flakes. Fry for 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the paste dries and darkens slightly.
Add the chicken pieces and brown on all sides for 5 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes and salt. Stir well. Cover and cook on low heat for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Remove the lid and cook for 5 minutes to reduce to a thick, clinging sauce. Serve with rice or parotta flatbread.

items.symptom: Spice paste smells raw after frying
items.cause: Not fried long enough or the heat was too low
items.fix: Fry the paste until it darkens and pulls away from the sides of the pan -- about 3 to 4 minutes

items.cause: Too much water evaporated during cooking
items.fix: Add 100ml of hot water and stir to loosen

items.cause: Lid was on for too long
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 10 minutes to reduce

content.text: Chettinad cuisine comes from the Sivaganga district of Tamil Nadu, home to the Nattukotai Chettiar merchant community. Their wealth from trade across Southeast Asia brought foreign spices into their cooking over centuries. Chicken Chettinad is now served across South India and in Indian restaurants worldwide.
